newsitem.title: USA: Calif. pension fund sells stock in lumber company.
newsitem.headline: Calif. pension fund sells stock in lumber company.

text.p: One of nation's largest public pension funds said Tuesday it sold all of its stock in MAXXAM Inc., a company under heavy fire from environmentalists who want to protect ancient trees in California.

The divestment, by the California State Teachers' Retirement System (STRS), was hailed by labor and environmental groups who have been lobbying the nation's largest public pension funds to sell their MAXXAM holdings.

Environmental groups said the divestment would help put pressure on Houston-based MAXXAM to protect old-growth redwoods within the Headwaters grove, the world's largest privately-owned ancient redwood forest located about 250 miles (400 kms) north of San Francisco.

"STRS' divestment makes it clear that public pension funds don't have to support the logging of our state tree," said Petaluma City, Calif., councilmember Matt Maguire, who sponsored a resolution calling for divestment.

James Mosman, the chief executive officer of STRS, said the $72 billion pension system sold 71,400 shares of MAXXAM, worth about $3.3 million. STRS had been MAXXAM's 10th largest institutional investor.
"It (the stock) didn't seem to be adding any economic value to the index," Mosman said, adding that pressure from environmental groups "was not the reason we sold the stock."
He said MAXXAM stock was held in the system's passive stock index. It was one of about 180 stocks dropped by the pension fund this year as part of its annual holdings review.
